narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Lit Console"**

SlipStream is a console lit by the Work it is showing. A Work's artwork sits blurred behind the page, and its hue runs through every surface and every ink, so a page about *Dune: Part Two* is a page in Dune's colour. Everything else holds still against that light. Red and amber are fixed alarms, green is a fixed all-clear, and live progress is white with a glow in the Work's hue. Glass blur belongs only to things that float. Lists, tables and cards are tinted translucent sheets with hairline edges, and nothing is drawn as a heavy box.

There is one theme, and it is dark. The Admin console is dense, built from A's layout in the direction ticket: a collapsible sidebar with live counts, a top bar with a ⌘K palette, and pages that open on a status sentence. The portal shares every token and component but runs at the Touch density, with B's poster-led layout and no machinery on screen. Geist sets everything. Geist Mono appears only in single values someone copies or compares down a column.

Motion is slow where light moves and quick where controls answer. The tint crossfades over 1.1s when focus moves to another Work. Buttons, switches and menus respond in about 200ms. Sheets and dialogs arrive on a spring.
keyCharacteristics: The Work in focus colours the page through a blurred ambient layer and two CSS properties, a hue and a saturation.
Fixed signal hues: red for failure, amber for warning, green for a passed check. None of them ever takes the tint.
Live is luminance. A running job is white with the Work's glow, and Met is solid white.
Translucent tinted surfaces, with glass blur only on floating chrome and overlays.
Two densities: Console for the Admin desktop shell, Touch for the Admin phone shell and the whole portal.
WCAG 2.2 AA is checked for every tint, and an ambient ceiling holds it.

rules.name: The Ambient Ceiling Rule
rules.body: After its layers composite, the brightest region of the ambient stays at or below relative luminance 0.053. Text sits directly on the ambient (the status sentence, breadcrumbs, section counts), and 0.053 is the brightest ground on which `ink-3` still clears 4.5:1 at every hue. Before showing a backdrop, measure its brightest region in the 24 × 36 sample and set the image's `brightness()` to hold the ceiling. A fixed `brightness(.6)`, as the prototypes used, does not hold it: a white backdrop under that filter composites to about 0.16.

rules.name: The Fixed Signal Rule
rules.body: Red, amber and green never take the tint, and the tint never takes their meaning. A signal is a solid chip, a dot, a solid card (red and amber only) or an icon. Never a thin coloured word on a tinted ground.

rules.name: The Luminance Is Live Rule
rules.body: Running work is white with the Work's glow. Met is solid white. A hue on screen means trouble or a passed check, never motion.

rules.name: The Never Alone Rule
rules.body: Every signal colour comes with an icon and a word. Red and green are the pair most often confused, so colour alone never carries the state.

rules.name: The Contrast Proof Rule
rules.body: Change a colour token only if the contrast check in `go run ./cmd/release lint` still passes. It sweeps 120 hues at six saturations, finds the ambient ceiling, requires it to equal the frontmatter's `ambient.ceiling`, and checks 32 ink and surface pairs at it. It reads the same parsed tokens the theme is generated from, and its pairs, named by token, live in `cmd/release/internal/tokens/contrast.go`.

rules.name: The Copy or Compare Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono sets a single value that someone copies or compares down a column: rates, sizes, durations, ETAs, percentages, timestamps in tables, release names, file names, file specs, paths, hashes, keys, addresses and ports. Everything else is Geist. Counts inside sentences, section counts, ordinals, step numbers and weekday labels are Geist with tabular numerals (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`). Apply Mono to the value's own element, never to a container that holds words.

rules.name: The Names Are Words Rule
rules.body: Names are never Mono. A Work, a Node, a Member, a Profile and a Target are names someone gave a thing, so they read as words, even when a Node's name looks like a hostname.

rules.name: The Container Rule
rules.body: A component reflows by container queries, not by viewport breakpoints. The Torrents table drops to four columns at 980px and becomes stacked cards at 620px, wherever it is drawn. An open Inspector narrows the page, and the table answers without a breakpoint of its own.

rules.name: The Floating Glass Rule
rules.body: Blur means "this floats above the page". Nothing that scrolls with the content is blurred. That covers live pills and chips on posters too.

rules.name: The Reduce Transparency Rule
rules.body: Under `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce`, every glass and translucent surface turns opaque at the same tint and lightness, and the ambient image hides, leaving the tint wash. Under `prefers-contrast: more`, `ink-2` and `ink-3` rise to `ink-1`, and hairlines rise to `hairline-strong` at full opacity. Under `forced-colors: active`, surfaces drop to system colours, and every state keeps its icon and its word.

rules.name: The Two Dots Rule
rules.body: The dots are always the Work's glow or the neutral blue. They never take a signal colour, and the mark never stands in for a status.

rules.name: The Reduce Motion Rule
rules.body: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the tint and backdrop swap at once, fills jump without the sheen, and overlays appear without travel. Page transitions and the sidebar cut. Spinners, steps, the PIN shake and canvas animations stop. No animation is exempt.

dos: **Do** take every surface and ink from the formulas in Colors, so a Work's hue reaches the whole page.
**Do** hold the ambient at or below relative luminance 0.053, measured per backdrop.
**Do** run `go run ./cmd/release lint` after changing any colour token, and keep its contrast check passing.
**Do** lead every watching page with a status sentence, then failures with their stage, cause and recovery, then live work.
**Do** show live work as white with the Work's glow, and Met as solid white.
**Do** pair every signal colour with an icon and a word.
**Do** use capsules for every control, at 32px in Console and 44px or more in Touch.
**Do** blur only what floats: bars, menus, popovers, the palette, the Inspector, Dialogs and sheets.
**Do** set rates, sizes, ETAs, timestamps, release names, paths and keys in Geist Mono, and everything else in Geist.
**Do** use the neutral ambient (214 / 14%) on every screen without a Work.
donts: **Don't** draw a light theme. v2 has one dark theme (parity row P-012 is excepted). Emails are the only light surface.
**Don't** tint red, amber or green, and don't let a failed Work drive the ambient.
**Don't** use green for Met, for live work or for a solid card. Green marks a passed check or a healthy thing, as a chip, dot or icon.
**Don't** add a fourth red. `fail-ink` covers failure text on glass, including the status sentence's link.
**Don't** set a name, a sentence, a count in prose or a step number in Geist Mono.
**Don't** use solid white for a selected segment or tab. Solid white means the primary action or Met.
**Don't** blur anything that scrolls with the content, such as a live pill or a chip on a poster.
**Don't** put text over a sharp backdrop unless a mask or scrim holds the ambient ceiling beneath it.
**Don't** use uppercase outside a failure card's key labels.
**Don't** use B's condensed display face (Big Shoulders Display). Geist sets the portal too.
**Don't** show Members any machinery: no Nodes, Targets, stages, releases or Conversions on the portal.
